[[File:Zverev MCM23 (20).jpg|thumb|upright=.7|[[Alexander Zverev]] is set to become the newest and 30th world No. 1 in November 2026 after Sinner ended his 2026 season due to injury. Zverev will also become the 20th year-end No. 1.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zverev clinches ATP Year-End No. 1 presented by PIF honours |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alexander-zverev-clinches-year-end-no-1-2026 |website=ATP Tour |date=12 October 2026}}</ref>]]

The PIF [[ATP rankings]]<ref>{{cite news |title=ATP & PIF announce multi-year strategic partnership to accelerate the growth of global tennis |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/atp-pif-strategic-partnership-february-2024 |access-date=6 March 2024 |work=ATP Tour |date=28 February 2024}}</ref> are the [[Association of Tennis Professionals]]' (ATP) merit-based system for determining the rankings in men's [[tennis]]. The top-ranked player is the player who, over the previous 52 weeks, has garnered the most ranking points on the [[ATP Tour]]. Points are awarded based on how far a player advances in tournaments and the category of those tournaments. The ATP has used a computerized system for determining the [[World number 1 ranked male tennis players|rankings]] since August 23, 1973.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How It All Began |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/corporate/history.aspx |access-date=July 20, 2012 |website=atpworldtour.com |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref> Starting in 1979, an updated rankings list is released at the beginning of each week. Since 1973, 29 players, have been ranked No. 1 by the ATP,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATP Rankings |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/rankings/singles |access-date=April 3, 2021 |website=atpworldtour.com |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=August 27, 2003 |title=ITF Tennis – How the Rankings Work |publisher=[[International Tennis Federation]] |url=http://www.itftennis.com/mens/startingout/rankrules.asp |access-date=June 11, 2009 |archive-date=December 19, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111219015531/http://www.itftennis.com/mens/startingout/rankrules.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref> of which 19 have been year-end No. 1.

== Ranking method ==
Since the introduction of the rankings, the method used to calculate a player's ranking points has changed several times. As of 2019, the rankings are calculated by totaling the points a player wins in his best eighteen tournaments, subject to certain restrictions. For top players the counting tournaments are the four [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] tournaments, the eight mandatory [[ATP Tour Masters 1000|ATP Masters]] tournaments, the non-mandatory ATP Masters 1000 event in Monte-Carlo, the player's best four eligible [[ATP Tour 500]] tournaments and his best two results from [[ATP Tour 250]] tournaments. Lower-ranked players who are not eligible for some or all of the top tournaments may include additional ATP 500 and ATP 250 events, and also [[ATP Challenger Tour]] and [[ITF Men's Circuit]] tournaments. Players who qualify for the year-end [[ATP Finals]] also include any points gained from the tournament in their total, increasing the number of tournaments counted to 19.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATP Ranking and Race Frequently Asked Questions |url=http://www.atpworldtour.com/Rankings/Rankings-FAQ.aspx |access-date=June 11, 2009 |website=atpworldtour.com |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref>

=== ATP singles ranking ===

'''1973–1982'''; ''ATP ranking's average system as introduced on August 23, 1973''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/heritage-1973-atp-rankings-celebration-part-i | title=The Rankings That Changed Tennis (Part I) &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis | work=ATP Tour }}</ref>

'''1983–1989'''; ''ATP ranking's average system with bonus points for beating top ranked players''.

'''1990–1999'''; '' ‘Best of 14’ ranking system, where a player’s best 14 results in the events counted''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/heritage-1973-atp-rankings-celebration-part-ii | title=The Rankings That Changed Tennis (Part II) &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis | work=ATP Tour }}</ref>

'''2000–2008'''; '' ‘Best of 18’ ranking system, where a player’s best 18 results in the events counted''.

'''2009–2019'''; '' A new point scale for ATP rankings to the ‘Best of 18’ ranking system''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/corporate/history | title=History &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis }}</ref>

'''2020{{efn|name=covid|The ATP rankings were frozen from March 23 to August 23, 2020, due to the [[Impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic on sports|COVID-19 pandemic]].}}–2021'''; '' ‘Best of 24-month’ ranking system from August 23, 2020 to August 9, 2021 for the two pandemic-impacted seasons''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/fedex-atp-rankings-adjustments-faq | title=FedEx ATP Rankings Adjustments FAQ &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis | work=ATP Tour }}</ref>
  
'''2022–2023'''; ''Normal ATP’s ranking system over a 52-week period restored since August 2021''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/rankings/rankings-faq.aspx | title=Rankings &#124; Pepperstone ATP Rankings FAQ &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis }}</ref>

'''2024–present'''; ''An updated ATP Rankings breakdown with increase in points at tour-level events since January 2024''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/2024-rankings-points-update | title=ATP Releases Pepperstone ATP Rankings Breakdown Updates &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis }}</ref>

== ATP records and distinctions ==
[[Novak Djokovic]] has spent the most weeks as world No. 1, a record total 428 weeks.<ref name="weeksrecord">{{Cite web |title=How A 'Golden Child' Became The Longest-Reigning Champ in ATP History |work=ATP Tour |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/celebrating-djokovic-record-311-weeks-at-world-no-1 |access-date=28 February 2022 |publisher=ATP}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-surpasses-graf-378-weeks-pepperstone-atp-rankings-february-2023 | title=Djokovic Surpasses Graf for Most Weeks at World No. 1 in History &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis }}</ref> [[Roger Federer]] has a record 237 consecutive weeks at No. 1.<ref name="History of No. 1">{{Cite web |title=Former No. 1s |url=https://www.atpworldtour.com/en/rankings/former-no-1s |access-date=October 13, 2018 |website=atpworldtour.com |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref> Djokovic also holds the record for the most year-end No. 1 finishes, achieving the feat for eight years (including the two [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports|pandemic-impacted]] seasons).<ref name="Djokovic2020">{{Cite web |title=Serbia's Novak Djokovic Clinches Year-End No. 1 in FedEx ATP Rankings; Equals Pete Sampras' Record of Six Year-End No. 1 Finishes &#124; ATP Tour &#124; Tennis |work=ATP Tour |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-clinches-2020-year-end-no-1-fedex-atp-rankings}}</ref><ref name="yearsrecord">{{Cite web |title=At Tennis' Summit, Novak Stands Alone |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/celebrating-djokovic-record-seven-finishes-at-year-end-no-1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220307171039/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/celebrating-djokovic-record-seven-finishes-at-year-end-no-1 |archive-date=7 March 2022 |publisher=ATP}}</ref> [[Pete Sampras]] held the year-end No. 1 ranking for a record six consecutive years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pete Sampras – Bio |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/players/pete-sampras/s402/bio |access-date=November 23, 2021 |website=atptour.com |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref><ref name="Sampras 6" />

[[Carlos Alcaraz]] is both the youngest world No. 1 ({{age in years, months, and days|2003|5|5|2022|9|12}}),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlos Alcaraz Becomes Youngest World No. 1 In Pepperstone ATP Rankings History {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alcaraz-climbs-to-world-no-1-us-open-2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912164653/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alcaraz-climbs-to-world-no-1-us-open-2022 |archive-date=2022-09-12 |website=ATP Tour}}</ref> and the youngest year-end No. 1 ({{age in years, months, and days|2003|5|5|2022|12|26}}).<ref name="youngest">{{Cite web |date=15 November 2022 |title=Alcaraz Youngest Year-End ATP No. 1 Presented By Pepperstone In History |url=https://www.nittoatpfinals.com/en/news/carlos-alcaraz-year-end-no-1-2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116023349/https://www.nittoatpfinals.com/en/news/carlos-alcaraz-year-end-no-1-2022 |archive-date=16 November 2022 |publisher=Nitto ATP Finals}}</ref> Djokovic is both the oldest world No. 1 ({{age in years, months, and days|1987|5|22|2024|6|9}})<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-04-01 |title=Djokovic to become the oldest No. 1 in PIF ATP Rankings history |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/djokovic-pif-atp-rankings-april-2024-oldest-no-1 |website=ATP Tour |language=en-US}}</ref> and the oldest year-end No. 1 ({{Age in years, months, and days|1987|5|22|2023|12|31}}).<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 November 2023 |title=Djokovic Clinches Record-Extending Eighth Year-End No. 1 Presented By Pepperstone |publisher=[[ATP Tour]] |url=https://www.nittoatpfinals.com/en/news/novak-djokovic-atp-year-end-no-1-presented-by-pepperstone-2023}}</ref>

Federer is the player with the longest time span ({{ayd|2004|2|2|2018|6|24}}) between his first and most recent dates at No. 1 (February 2, 2004 – June 24, 2018),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Federer Smashes Records in Return to No. 1 |work=ATP World Tour |url=http://www./.com/en/news/federer-historic-return-to-number-one |access-date=February 19, 2018 |publisher=[[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP)}}</ref> while [[Rafael Nadal]] is the only player to hold the top ranking in three different decades,<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 June 2026 |title=From Nastase to Djokovic to Sinner: Remarkable facts about ATP No. 1 Club members {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=http://www.atptour.com/en/news/atp-no-1-club-docuseries-29-facts |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261015223721/https://www.atptour.com/en/news/atp-no-1-club-docuseries-29-facts |archive-date=2026-10-15 |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=ATP Tour |language=en}}</ref> spanning {{ayd|2008|8|18|2020|2|2}} (August 18, 2008 — February 2, 2020), 46 weeks in the 2000s, 159 weeks in the 2010s, and 4 weeks in the 2020s. Djokovic has the longest time span (12 years) between his first and last year-end No. 1 finish (2011–2023), and is the only player to be ranked No. 1 at least once in a year for 13 different years (2011–2016 & 2018–2024).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berkok |first=John |date=2023-02-02 |title=Novak Djokovic: 22 Stats For His 22nd Grand Slam Title |url=https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/novak-djokovic-22-stats-for-his-22nd-grand-slam-australian-open |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=Tennis.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Federer holds the record of wire-to-wire No. 1 for three consecutive calendar years. Since 1973 when the [[ATP rankings]] started, there have been 13 years in which one player held the top spot for the entire year: [[Jimmy Connors]] in 1975, 1976, and 1978; Lendl in 1986 and 1987; Pete Sampras in 1994 and 1997; Hewitt in 2002; Federer in 2005, 2006, and 2007; and Djokovic in 2015 and 2021. In contrast, 1999 saw five players hold the No. 1 ranking (the most in any single year): Sampras, [[Carlos Moyá]], [[Yevgeny Kafelnikov]], [[Andre Agassi]], and [[Pat Rafter|Patrick Rafter]]. The 1999 season is also the only season with 3 players making their No. 1 debut, with only 4 other seasons seeing 2 players making their No. 1 debuts, 1974, 2000, 2003, and 2022.

Prior to 2009, Federer accumulated the most year-end ATP ranking points in any season, with 8,370 points in [[2006 ATP Tour|2006]]. Since the introduction of a new point scale for the ATP rankings from 2009, Djokovic achieved the same feat with 16,585 ranking points in [[2015 ATP Tour|2015]] season. Djokovic holds the distinction of having 16,950 ranking points on June 6, 2016, the most ATP points ever accumulated by any player since 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ATP Tour {{!}} Best of the Decade: Records & Achievements {{!}} Nadal, Djokovic, Federer Lead The Way {{!}} ATP Tour {{!}} Tennis |url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/best-of-decade-records-achievements |access-date=2022-09-11 |website=ATP Tour}}</ref>

[[John McEnroe]] held the No. 1 ranking a record 14 times, Sampras and Djokovic are the only two other players to have held it 10 or more times, with 11 and 10 stints respectively. Rafter spent the least time at number 1 (one week).

Two players, [[Ivan Lendl]] and [[Marcelo Ríos]], have reached No. 1 without previously having won a [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] singles title.<ref name="Rios No. 1">{{Cite news |last=Finn |first=Robin |date=March 30, 1998 |title=Tennis; Rios Dismantles Agassi and Seizes No. 1 Ranking |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/30/sports/tennis-rios-dismantles-agassi-and-seizes-no-1-ranking.html?pagewanted=all |access-date=July 21, 2012 |quote=Rios...is the first man to earn the ranking without winning a Grand Slam tournament since Ivan Lendl in 1983.}}</ref> Lendl reached No. 1 on February 21, 1983, but did not win his first Grand Slam title until the [[1984 French Open]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=June 18, 1984 |title=Worthy of really high fives |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=CNN |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1984/06/18/638109/worthy-of-really-high-fives |access-date=June 11, 2009 |archive-date=August 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190807220529/https://www.si.com/vault/1984/06/18/638109/worthy-of-really-high-fives |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ríos reached No. 1 on March 30, 1998, but retired without ever having won a Grand Slam title, making him the only No. 1 player with that distinction.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilstein |first=Steve |date=February 1, 1998 |title=Korda takes Australian Open title |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/sports/tennis/longterm/1998/ausopen/articles/launch/menfinal.htm |access-date=June 11, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Player biography – Marcelo Ríos |url=http://www.itftennis.com/procircuit/players/player/profile.aspx?playerid=10005756 |access-date=June 11, 2009 |publisher=[[International Tennis Federation]] |archive-date=January 6, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170106212031/http://www.itftennis.com/procircuit/players/player/profile.aspx?playerid=10005756 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Year-end No. 1 players ==
[[File:Novak Djokovic Eastbourne tennis 2017 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=.7|alt=Novak Djokovic serving the ball|[[Novak Djokovic]] holds an all-time record of eight year-end No. 1 finishes.]]
[[File:Pete Sampras.jpg|thumb|upright=.7|alt=A tennis player holds a racket in his hand and prepares to serve|[[Pete Sampras]] finished six consecutive years as year-end No. 1 in the 1990s.]]
[[File:The Federer Technique - Oz Open 2014.jpg|thumb|upright=.7|alt= Federer serving at the [[Australian Open]] in 2014|[[Roger Federer]] finished as the year-end No. 1 for four consecutive years and in total five years in the 2000s.]]
[[File:John McEnroe (1979)-2.jpg|thumb|upright=.7|alt=John McEnroe playing tennis|[[John McEnroe]] finished as the year-end No. 1 for four consecutive years in the 1980s.]]
The ATP year-end No. 1 (ATP Player of the Year), in recent decades, it has been determined as the player who ends the year as world No. 1 in the ATP rankings. Prior to the early 1990s this was not always the case, in some instances the "ATP Player of the Year" and the Year-end No. 1 in the rankings were different players (1975, 1976, 1977, 1978, 1982, 1989). [[Novak Djokovic]] holds the ATP record of eight year-end No. 1 finishes.<ref name="yearsrecord" /> Overall, 20 players have achieved the year-end No. 1 ranking. Ten of them have achieved this more than once, of which five ([[Ivan Lendl|Lendl]], [[Roger Federer|Federer]], [[Novak Djokovic|Djokovic]], [[Rafael Nadal|Nadal]] and [[Carlos Alcaraz|Alcaraz]]) have done so in non-consecutive years. Lendl and Federer were the first two players who would regain the Year-end No. 1. Nadal and Djokovic would regain the Year-end No. 1 four times. Six players have stayed at No. 1 in the ATP rankings for every week of the calendar year. [[Jimmy Connors|Connors]] and Federer have done so in three years, Connors non-consecutively and Federer consecutively.
{{Legend|#ffffcf|text=<nowiki>*</nowiki>|Player was ranked No. 1 throughout the entire calendar year.}}
